correctness.rationale: Character-square Euler products provide an exact proof in all degrees and all binary finite fields. In the nontrivial-multiplicative-character sector the squarefree series has degree at most one, so all degree-n coefficients for n≥2 vanish. The remaining additive sectors yield T_n and A_n explicitly, and character inversion yields the formula. Direct exhaustive gcd computations over four finite fields support the result without replacing universal proof.

originality.rationale: Five semantic published-finding corpus queries, searches of trace/norm and prescribed-factorization literature, checks against own 29 accessible current-week claim statements, and targeted full-text material produced no directly equivalent or stronger accessible theorem. Prior claims on finite fields concern irreducibles, unrestricted squarefree totals, or initial coefficients only, whereas this result imposes initial trace and nonzero constant jointly for all squarefree polynomials. A related-objects paper was inaccessible beyond abstract and remains explicitly unresolved; best-knowledge originality is conditional on this residual risk.
residual_risks: Gao–Kuttner–Wang (2021) is highly plausible stronger coverage; only its abstract could be inspected, and "related objects" might include squarefree coefficient-conditioned counts.
Classical finite-field character-Euler-product arguments might yield equivalent squarefree trace/norm formulas in older unindexed literature; a failed search is not a proof of novelty.
No independent audit or external certificate was performed.

value.rationale: The squarefree locus with jointly fixed trace and norm is a natural arithmetic family relevant to polynomial generation and finite-field factor statistics. This gives a simultaneous exact classification for every binary finite field and degree >=2, proving unexpected independence of all nonzero constants and a parity-controlled exactly one-unit bias between trace sectors. Neither global squarefree totals nor simple coefficient-scaling symmetry determines this distribution, and the formula exposes a specific characteristic-two cancellation.
